https://www.dw.com/en/us-multiple-dead-i.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5I8s0 The In-N-Out Burger restaurant in Twin Falls opened just about a week earlier on July 24 [FILE: April 2023] Image: Taidgh Barron/ZUMA/picture alliance Advertisement Multiple people were killed and others were injured after a gunman opened fire at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant in a city in the northwestern US state of Idaho. The shooting unfolded near a busy shopping area in Twin Falls where hundreds of people were present, police chief Matthew Hicks said in a news conference. The suspected shooter was among the dead, Hicks said. Police were still trying to determine the shooter's identity and motive. Local media broadcast video footage from the scene showing what appeared to be a young man carrying a long gun outside the restaurant that had only been open for a week at the Twin Falls location. Police to confirm exact number of fatalities The shooting at the burger chain "resulted in fatalities" but authorities were still working to determine the number of victims, Hicks said. "We are working to try to ascertain his identity and the motivations behind [the shooting] and we'll be able to figure that out in the next coming days," he said, adding that it was a "very chaotic scene." Local public radio station KTVB reported that three people were killed and two were injured. A city spokesperson said the number of victims is expected to be higher. Multiple people hospitalized after shooting at Idaho In-N-Out Police said multiple people were taken to St. Luke's Magic Valley Medical Center. Hospital spokesperson Taylor Marschner said in a statement that it was "working closely with law enforcement and emergency responders as they manage the situation." Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is about 130 miles (205 kilometers) southeast of Boise and about 75 miles (120 kilometers) north of the Nevada border. https://www.politico.eu/article/nobel-pr.text: Welcome to Declassified, a weekly humor column . This column has, once again, been overlooked for the Nobel Prize in Literature — although there’s still hope for the Peace Prize. Asked by Declassified if it could justify this blatant discrimination, the Nobel committee hung up the phone. Advertisement Advertisement Politicians can, of course, make great writers, and several have won Nobel’s literature prize, including Britain’s Winston Churchill in 1953, and Peru’s Mario Vargas Llosa in 2010. The latter — who ran for president in 1990 — won the prize “for his cartography of structures of power and his trenchant images of the individual’s resistance, revolt, and defeat.” But has he ever referred to British Conservative grandee Jacob Rees-Mogg as a “Haunted Pencil”? No, he has not. There are, however, a lot of very bad books written by politicians. Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson — very much the “Winston Churchill if you ordered him off Temu” — published a book in 2004 called “Seventy-Two Virgins — A Comedy of Errors” (the last four words also being the summary of his Covid policy) about a terrorist group targeting the U.S. president on a visit to London. It was described in the Guardian some 15 years later — after Johnson became prime minister — as ” sexist, racist, fundamentally undiplomatic.” But the undisputed king when it comes to politicians letting out their inner writer is France. In 2023, Bruno Le Maire , then the country’s economy and finance minister, published the novel “ Fugue Américaine ,” which drew instant criticism and mockery, mainly because of an explicit sex scene (unhappy French people were quick to point out that they had been screwed by the government for years). Then there’s Marlène Schiappa, former government minister and writer of raunchy books under the pen name Marie Minelli, with titles such as “ Osez les sexfriends ,” “ Sexe, mensonge et banlieues chaudes ” and “ Comment transformer votre mec en Brad Pitt en 30 jours .” When she was junior social affairs minister, Schiappa appeared on the cover of Playboy, although she was not naked in the magazine (great news for those who buy Playboy only for the articles). Advertisement Advertisement Former President Valéry Giscard d’Estaing published several erotic novels, including “ La Princesse et le Président ,” which features sex scenes set in the presidential palace. But perhaps the most intriguing of all is current President Emmanuel Macron, whose erotic novel about the early days of his romance with Brigitte has, alas, never seen the light of day. Perhaps he’s keeping it back for political gain and will promise to publish the steamy tome if the people of France promise to vote for a centrist candidate in April’s election. The £550 Big Shot wrapped up on October 13, and there was a familiar name at the top of the payout table: the legendary John Duthie . A compact field of 98 entrants built a £47,020 prize pool, which far exceeded the £30,000 guarantee. The nine-handed final table awarded its players prizes ranging from £1,300 to £12,470, and Duthie took home the largest sum. £550 Big Shot Final Table Results Rank Player Prize 1 John Duthie £12,470 2 Rafael Robles £10,500 3 Ernst Soederkvist £6,450 4 Michael O'Brien £4,370 5 Henry Fulcher £3,010 6 Norman Butterfield £2,160 7 Joe Hindry £1,670 8 Max Winberg £1,410 9 Philippe Souki £1,300 Philippe Souki , a player with over $2.5 million in live tournament cashes, fell in ninth before Max Winberg fell in eighth, his first recorded live score in four years. Seventh place went to Joe Hindry , with Norman Butterfield crashing out in sixth place. Henry Fulcher's £3,010 fifth-place prize represented a new career-high for him, and when Michael O'Brien and Ernst Soederkvist bowed out, Duthie locked horns and butted heads with Rafael Robles in a heads-up battle for the title, trophy, and top prize. Robles fell at the final hurdle and earned £10,500, leaving Duthie to capture the title and £12,470. Maksims Uksovs Wins the £250 PLO 4-Card Event Maksims Uksovs The £250 PLO 4-Card tournament drew 61 entrants, creating a £12,750 prize pool that the final eight players shared. After Sebastien Jung , Howard Smith , Fabio Esposito , and Hussani Alkhuzai fell by the wayside, the remaining four players locked in more than £1,200 for their efforts. Frenchman Aurelien Martin collected £1,270 for his fourth-place finish. The 2023 WPT500 UK champion, Aleksandrs Golubevs , busted in third for £1,850 before Maksims Uskovs defeated Lin Chen heads-up. The bulk of the £114,560 prize pool remains to be won, including a first-place prize of £26,220. At the start of the final table, an anonymous player going by the initials "P.C." is the player to catch. They sit down with 1,615,000 chips. Two other players, Guang Yang (1,295,000) and Richard Broda (1,180,000), return to their seats as chip millionaires and will fancy their chances of Mini Main glory. Lithuanian Tomas Dailidonis (965,000) lurks just outside the top three, while in-form Indian Pranav Agarwal (640,000) sits down sixth in chips at the restart. £340 Mini Main Final Table Chip Counts Rank Player Chip Count 1 P.C. 1,615,000 2 Guang Yang 1,295,000 3 Richard Broda 1,180,000 4 Tomas Dailidonis 965,000 5 Michael Long 955,000 6 Pranav Agarwal 640,000 7 Greg Hawes 620,000 8 Hanyang Shi 585,000 9 Artin Bazai 185,000 £340 Mini Main Final Table Payouts £26,220 £17,530 £11,490 £7,580 £5,170 £3,730 £2,860 £2,300 £1,900 PokerNews Coverage of the High Roller and Main Event Begins October 14 Gang Wang: Reigning 888LIVE London Main Event champion The PokerNews live reporting team has arrived in London and is gearing up to bring you live and exclusive coverage of the £2,000 High Roller and the eagerly anticipated £1,250 Main Event . Last year, Nuno Duarte took down the High Roller, which had a £1,650 buy-in, for £43,510 after leaving a trail of 114 foes in his dust. Gang Wang is the reigning 888LIVE London Main Event champion. Wang topped a 367-strong field, including defeating Calogero Morreale heads-up, to win £86,600.
